title: Moderate gap: localized polynomial ring vs polynomial ring — license for the cited LS formula

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** solution.tex §1.1 (choice $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]_{(x_1,\dots,x_n)}$) and §1.2 (claim $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R A\cong A^n$ free on $dx_i$).

The classical Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger $\operatorname{coker}(J)$ statement is normally stated for $R$ a **polynomial** ring; the solution uses its **localization** at the irrelevant maximal ideal. To legitimately invoke the standard theorem one must justify that the localized presentation computes the same $T^1$. The needed facts are true but omitted:

1. $\Omega_{R/k}$ for the localization is the localization of $\Omega_{k[x]/k}$, hence free with basis $dx_1,\dots,dx_n$, and $\Omega_{R/k}\otimes_R A=\Omega_{k[x]/k}\otimes_{k[x]}A$. (Differentials commute with localization — Matsumura.)

2. If $A=S/J$ with $S=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring and $J=\ker(\pi_S)$, then since $A$ is local Artinian (its own localization at the unique prime, the image of $(x)$) one has
$$R/I=(S/J)_{(x)}=S/J=A,\qquad\text{hence } I=J\cdot R,$$
so the $A$-modules $I/I^2$ and $\Omega_R\otimes_R A$ agree with those computed from the polynomial presentation. Therefore the two presentations give the **identical** $\operatorname{coker}(J)$.

**How to close.** Add one short paragraph stating (1) and (2). Difficulty: low. But it is genuinely needed, otherwise the appeal to the (polynomial-base) standard theorem is not literally licensed.
